findings.contract_quote: §8.2.9: 'If available, the insurance policies required by this contract may be combined with Commercial Umbrella Insurance policies to meet the minimum limit requirements.' §8.2.11 (Auto): 'Commercial/Business Automobile Liability insurance with a combined single limit for bodily injury and property damage of not less than $2,000,000 each occurrence' (no inline mention of umbrella attachment).
findings.policy_quote: [NO UMBRELLA POLICY IN PROGRAM]
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.9 contains program-level umbrella permission ('may be combined with Commercial Umbrella ... to meet the minimum limit requirements'). §8.2.11 (Auto) and §8.2.13 (Cyber) do not inline-mention umbrella attachment, while §8.2.10 (CGL) explicitly does. Strict reading: umbrella permission only applies to lines that inline-acknowledge it (CGL only). Permissive reading: §8.2.9 covers all lines and umbrella stacking is OK on Auto. This is the same ambiguity the audit instructions flag as a Needs Review trigger. Independent of this question, the underlying Auto limit shortfall is a separate Bad/Ugly finding (finding-009).
findings.plain_english: Whether you can use an umbrella to bridge from $1M Auto to $2M Auto under the Maricopa contract is genuinely ambiguous. Maricopa County's Risk Manager needs to confirm in writing how they read it. Until then, treat Auto as needing $2M at the primary level OR as needing both higher primary AND a confirmation letter.
findings.recommendation: Email Maricopa County Risk Management (301 W Jefferson, Suite 910, Phoenix) with a direct question: 'Does §8.2.9 permit Commercial Umbrella to satisfy the §8.2.11 Auto $2M CSL requirement, or must the $2M be at the primary Auto layer?' Document the reply in the file. In parallel, scope a $2M primary Auto quote so you can elect the cleaner path if Maricopa says umbrella stacking is not permitted.

findings.requirement_type: Maricopa Cyber $5M Minimum — Umbrella Attachment Ambiguous
findings.contract_quote: §8.2.9: 'If available, the insurance policies required by this contract may be combined with Commercial Umbrella Insurance policies to meet the minimum limit requirements.' §8.2.13 (Cyber): 'Cyber, Network Security and Privacy Liability Insurance with a limit of not less than $5,000,000 per occurrence' (no inline mention of umbrella).
findings.policy_quote: [NO CYBER POLICY AND NO UMBRELLA IN PROGRAM]
findings.gap_description: Same ambiguity as finding-010 but for Cyber. In practice, almost no Commercial Umbrella follows form over Cyber/Privacy — Cyber is typically a standalone tower. The cleanest reading is that §8.2.13 must be met at the primary Cyber layer with $5M. Standalone $5M Cyber + optional Cyber Excess is the market answer.
findings.plain_english: Even if Maricopa allows umbrella to count toward Cyber, almost no umbrella actually covers cyber claims. Plan to meet the $5M Cyber requirement at the primary Cyber layer.
findings.recommendation: Bind $5M primary Cyber per finding-003. Do not rely on §8.2.9 umbrella language to cover Cyber.

findings.requirement_type: Additional Insured — CGL Blanket via CG 20 10 + CG 20 37 (Limited by Classification)
findings.contract_quote: ADDITIONAL INSURED STATUS: The COUNTY, its officers, directors, officials, employees, and volunteers are to be endorsed as additional insureds as respects: liability arising out of activities performed by or on behalf of the CONTRACTOR; products and completed operations of the CONTRACTOR; premises owned, occupied or used by the CONTRACTOR; or automobiles owned, leased, hired or borrowed by the CONTRACTOR. The coverage shall contain no endorsed limitations on the scope of protection afforded to the COUNTY ... (Sacramento §VII.A); ... shall name County, its agents, representatives, officers, directors, officials, and employees as additional insureds. (Maricopa §8.2.7)
findings.contract_file: Sacramento County Appendix G; Maricopa County contract
findings.policy_quote: CG 20 10 12 19: 'ALL PARTIES WHERE REQUIRED BY A WRITTEN CONTRACT PROVIDED SUCH CONTRACT WAS EXECUTED PRIOR TO LOSS' ... 'A. Section II — Who Is An Insured is amended to include as an additional insured the person(s) or organization(s) shown in the Schedule, but only with respect to liability for "bodily injury", "property damage" or "personal and advertising injury" caused, in whole or in part
findings.gap_description: On its face, the AI structure (CG 20 10 + CG 20 37 ongoing + completed ops, blanket-by-contract trigger) is correct and satisfies Sacramento §VII.A and Maricopa §8.2.7. Two material limitations: (1) coverage 'will not be broader than required by contract' and limits are capped at the lesser of contract-required or policy-available — both standard 2013-edition language but worth flagging because Sacramento §VII.A says 'no endorsed limitations,' which arguably this clause is. (2) The Classification Limitation (00 GL0713, Pg 39) means AI status only attaches to claims arising out of declared classifications (security/patrol/alarms/detective). For claims arising out of election services operations, the AI extension is meaningless because the underlying coverage doesn't apply. The 'caused in whole or in part by' language meets Sacramento's 'arising out of' broad-AI standard.
findings.plain_english: The AI endorsements look right on paper — blanket, ongoing AND completed operations, triggered by written contract. But because the GL only covers security guard work, the AI status only protects the County for security guard claims. If a county sues over an election services issue, the County's AI status under this policy gives them nothing because the policy doesn't cover that exposure to begin with.
findings.recommendation: Re-confirm AI status on the new operations-CGL once placed (per finding-001). Verify CG 20 10 + CG 20 37 (or broader equivalents like CG 20 33 + CG 20 38) attach to the operations-CGL with blanket-by-contract trigger and 'arising out of' or 'caused in whole or in part by' language. For Sacramento, push for an AI form WITHOUT the contract-required-limit cap if possible — or note in the file that the standard 2013 edition is industry custom and Sacramento has accepted it on prior projects.
discoveryQuestions: When you certify Sacramento or Maricopa as an Additional Insured, does the broker attach the actual CG 20 10 and CG 20 37 endorsement copies to the COI, or just reference them?
Has either County ever pushed back on AI language as too narrow ('not broader than required by contract')?
Do you understand that AI status on the security-guard GL won't help the County if a claim is about election services rather than security guards?

findings.requirement_type: Additional Insured — Auto Blanket via 461-0478
findings.contract_quote: ADDITIONAL INSURED STATUS: ... or automobiles owned, leased, hired or borrowed by the CONTRACTOR. (Sacramento §VII.A) ... shall name County, its agents, representatives, officers, directors, officials, and employees as additional insureds. (Maricopa §8.2.7)
findings.policy_quote: 461-0478 12 12 — Blanket Additional Insured - Primary and Non-Contributory: 'Any person or organization required by written contract, written agreement or written permit ... executed before the accident.' Primary and non-contributory included; AI limit is lesser of contract-specified or policy limit. Exceptions: sole negligence of AI; non-owned/non-trailer auto driven by AI; when AI is AI under another liability policy.
findings.gap_description: The Hanover Auto policy provides blanket Additional Insured status with primary and non-contributory built in via Form 461-0478. Trigger is 'written contract/agreement/permit executed before the accident' — meets both Sacramento and Maricopa AI requirements. Three carve-outs are standard (AI sole negligence, AI driving non-owned auto, AI under another policy). Strong AI compliance on the Auto line.
findings.plain_english: The Auto policy automatically names the County as an Additional Insured whenever a written contract requires it — and adds the primary-and-noncontributory feature in the same endorsement. This is exactly what both county contracts ask for.
findings.recommendation: Maintain. Note for COI issuance: Form 461-0478 should be referenced on the COI Description of Operations and the actual endorsement copy attached per Sacramento §I and Maricopa §8.2.14.

findings.requirement_type: Primary & Noncontributory — CGL via CG 20 01

(Sacramento §VII.C); Contractor's insurance shall be primary insurance as respects County, and any insurance or self-insurance maintained by County shall not contribute to it. (Maricopa §8.2.4)
findings.policy_quote: CG 20 01 12 19 — Primary And Noncontributory – Other Insurance Condition: triggered when (1) the AI is a Named Insured under such other insurance AND (2) there is a written contract requiring P&NC.
findings.gap_description: The standard ISO Primary & Noncontributory endorsement (CG 20 01) is on the CGL. It satisfies both Sacramento §VII.C and Maricopa §8.2.4 when triggered by written contract. Same Classification Limitation issue applies (security ops only) — but the P&NC mechanism is structurally compliant.
findings.plain_english: The P&NC endorsement is in place on the GL. Standard ISO form. When the contract requires it, this policy goes first and the County's insurance stays back.
findings.recommendation: Maintain on operations-CGL once placed. CG 20 01 should be carried forward to any replacement or supplemental GL.

findings.requirement_type: Primary & Noncontributory — Auto via 461-0478
findings.contract_quote: Sacramento §VII.C; Maricopa §8.2.4
findings.policy_quote: 461-0478 12 12 — Blanket Additional Insured - Primary and Non-Contributory: P&NC bundled directly into the AI endorsement.
findings.gap_description: Auto P&NC is bundled into the same blanket AI endorsement. Compliant with both county contracts.
findings.plain_english: Auto P&NC is built into the same AI endorsement. Covered.

findings.requirement_type: Waiver of Subrogation — CGL Missing
findings.contract_quote: The policies required hereunder, except Workers' Compensation and Errors and Omissions, shall contain a waiver of transfer of rights of recovery (subrogation) against County. (Maricopa §8.2.8) — and Sacramento RMF practice requires WoS where contractually demanded.
findings.policy_quote: [NO BLANKET WAIVER OF SUBROGATION ENDORSEMENT IDENTIFIED IN ARCH CGL FORM SCHEDULE OR ENDORSEMENT LIST]
findings.policy_page: N/A — checklist field 'waiver_of_subrogation' = false; waiver_of_subrogation_page = null
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.8 expressly requires WoS on GL (excluding only WC and E&O from that requirement). The Arch CGL endorsement schedule (Pgs 8 onward through CG 21 96, CG 40 35, etc.) contains no Waiver of Transfer of Rights of Recovery endorsement. This is a direct contract non-conformance — independent of the Classification Limitation issue. Cross-state RMF practice (broker target) is blanket WoS where required by written contract.
findings.plain_english: Maricopa County's contract requires that your GL carrier waive its right to come after the County after paying a claim. Your GL doesn't have that endorsement. If a worker is hurt at a county site and your GL pays, the carrier could turn around and sue the County for reimbursement — exactly what the County is trying to prevent. This is a direct contract violation.
findings.recommendation: Add a Blanket Waiver of Transfer of Rights of Recovery (Subrogation) endorsement to the CGL — typically free or nominal cost. ISO equivalent: CG 24 04 (Waiver of Transfer of Rights of Recovery Against Others to Us). When the operations-CGL is placed (per finding-001), include blanket WoS as a binding requirement.
discoveryQuestions: Has the Maricopa COI ever been issued claiming Waiver of Subrogation on GL — and if so, do you know what endorsement supports that representation?
If your GL carrier subrogates against Maricopa after paying a guard-related claim, do you understand that puts you in material breach of the contract?
Is your broker willing to bind a no-cost CG 24 04 endorsement for the remainder of this policy term, or do we wait until renewal?

findings.requirement_type: Waiver of Subrogation — Auto Blanket via 461-0500
findings.contract_quote: Maricopa §8.2.8; Sacramento §VIII (WC); RMF practice for Auto WoS where contractually required.
findings.policy_quote: 461-0500 11 13 — Waiver of Transfer of Rights of Recovery Against Others to Us: 'BLANKET WHERE REQUIRED BY WRITTEN CONTRACT. Applies only to extent subrogation waived prior to accident or loss under contract.' Reinforced by 461-0155 Item 18: 'BLANKET WAIVER OF SUBROGATION preserved through insured contract/written agreement/permit prior to accident.'
findings.gap_description: Auto policy carries a true blanket Waiver of Subrogation triggered by written contract executed before the accident. Backstopped by 461-0155 Broadening Item 18. Strong compliance with Maricopa §8.2.8.
findings.plain_english: Your Auto policy automatically waives subrogation against any party where a written contract requires it. Maricopa is covered.
findings.recommendation: Maintain.

findings.requirement_type: Cancellation Notice — 30-Day Designated Entity NOC (Maricopa)
findings.contract_quote: Contractor's insurance shall not be permitted to expire, be suspended, be canceled, or be materially changed for any reason without 30 days prior written notice to Maricopa County. Contractor must provide to Maricopa County, within two business days of receipt, if they receive notice of a policy that has been or will be suspended, canceled, materially changed for any reason, has expired, or will be expiring.
findings.policy_quote: GL: AZ Changes IL 02 58 — '10 days nonpayment / 45 days other reasons (after 60 days in force).' No Designated Entity NOC endorsement found on GL. Auto: 401-1235 12 14 Notice of Cancellation to Designated Entity(s) — 30-day notice with multi-page schedule listing City of Boulder, Coconino County, Amazon, El Paso County, San Luis Obispo County, State of Colorado, NY State OGS — but Maricopa County is NOT listed on the schedule. 461-0155 Item 1 extends Auto to 60 days for non-nonpayment.
findings.policy_page: GL Pgs 11, 14 (no DEN); Auto Pgs 44–46 (401-1235 schedule)
findings.gap_description: Maricopa §8.2.15 requires 30-day notice and 'material change' notice on ALL required policies — likely needs Designated Entity NOC endorsement (e.g., CG 20 12 / CG 02 24). On the GL: no Designated Entity NOC endorsement is in place; AZ statutory provides 45 days for other reasons but only AFTER 60 days in force, and there is no carrier obligation to notify Maricopa County directly. On the Auto: Form 401-1235 provides 30-day Designated Entity NOC, but the schedule lists 7 entities — Maricopa County is NOT one of them. The Maricopa contract has been in effect since 11/01/21 yet Maricopa was never added to the Auto NOC schedule. Sacramento §VI.A.2 takes a softer approach (Contractor self-notifies County immediately, plus 10-day pre-anniversary renewal evidence) — that obligation is on the Contractor, not the carrier, but should still be calendared.
findings.plain_english: Maricopa wants 30 days' direct notice from the carrier if your insurance is canceled or materially changed. Your GL doesn't have that endorsement at all. Your Auto policy has the right endorsement type — but Maricopa isn't on the list of counties it notifies. Other counties (Coconino, El Paso, etc.) are listed, but somehow Maricopa was missed. Practical risk: if the carrier cancels mid-term, Maricopa never gets the carrier-direct notice the contract requires, and the contractor self-notify obligation kicks in too late.
findings.recommendation: (1) Add Maricopa County as a Designated Entity NOC recipient on the Auto policy (Form 401-1235) at next renewal — endorsement is no-cost. Also add: 'BLANKET WHERE REQUIRED BY WRITTEN CONTRACT' wording if available. (2) Bind Designated Entity NOC endorsement on operations-CGL once placed (and on the security-guard CGL if Maricopa applies it) — typically CG 02 24 or carrier-equivalent. (3) Operationally: calendar the Sacramento 10-day pre-anniversary renewal evidence requirement (Sacramento §VI.A.2) and the 2-business-day pass-through notice obligation (Maricopa §8.2.15).
discoveryQuestions: Look at Page 44–46 of the Auto policy — Maricopa County isn't on the Designated Entity Notice list, but Coconino County is. Do you know why Maricopa was excluded?
Does Run-Test have a centralized list of all contract-required cancellation-notice recipients, or has this been managed contract-by-contract?
What's your renewal calendar discipline for the Sacramento 10-day-pre-anniversary evidence-of-renewal requirement — is anyone in your office responsible for sending those?

findings.requirement_type: 90-Day Cancellation Notice — Broker Benchmark vs Carrier Provisions
findings.contract_quote: [Broker RMF target — General All Policies #1: 90-day notice of cancellation is the broker benchmark.] Maricopa §8.2.15 requires 30 days carrier notice; Sacramento §VI.A.2 puts notice obligation on Contractor, not carrier.
findings.policy_quote: GL: 10 days nonpayment / 45 days other reasons (AZ statutory IL 02 58). Auto: 10 days nonpayment / 60 days other reasons (461-0155 Item 1).
findings.gap_description: Broker RMF target is 90-day NOC. GL provides 45 days max (after 60 days in force); Auto provides 60 days max via 461-0155 Item 1. Both fall short of the 90-day broker benchmark, though Auto's 60 days exceeds Maricopa's 30-day contract minimum. This is an enhancement opportunity, not a contract violation per se.
findings.plain_english: As a best-practice matter, brokers push for 90 days' cancellation notice across the program so the client has time to replace coverage if a carrier walks. You currently have 45 days on GL and 60 days on Auto. That meets the contracts, but it doesn't meet the broker target.
findings.recommendation: At renewal, push carriers for 90-day cancellation amendments — often available as a no-cost or low-cost endorsement on standard market policies. Document the request even if denied so the file shows the broker advocated for the higher standard.
discoveryQuestions: If your GL carrier non-renewed you 45 days out, do you have a market relationship that could place coverage in time, or would you scramble?
Has Patriot ever pushed Hanover or Arch for 90-day NOC amendments on prior renewals, and what was the response?

findings.requirement_type: Unintentional E&O — CGL Endorsement Present
findings.contract_quote: [RMF General §2 — Unintentional Errors and Omissions giveback should be on every policy.]
findings.policy_quote: 00 GL1050 00 01 25 — Unintentional Errors or Omissions: 'Insured's failure to disclose hazards at inception not prejudicial unless intentional.'
findings.gap_description: Unintentional E&O endorsement is in place on the CGL via Form 00 GL1050. Protects against inadvertent failure to disclose a hazard, location, or operation at inception.
findings.plain_english: If you forgot to mention a location or operation at policy inception by accident, the carrier can't use that to deny a claim. This endorsement protects you from honest mistakes at the application stage. It's in place.
findings.recommendation: Maintain. Carry forward to any replacement or supplemental CGL.

findings.contract_quote: [RMF General §2]
findings.policy_quote: 461-0155 Business Auto Coverage Broadening Endorsement, Item 19 — Unintentional failure to disclose.
